name: Black tea
caffeine: From the leaf itself: commonly 40 to 70 mg in an 8 oz cup, less than drip coffee, moved by leaf, heat and steep time.

house.ask: Tea is not printed on the menus: ask at lineup whether the bar pours a black tea, which brand, bag or loose leaf, pot or cup, and the price.

what: Black tea is the leaf of Camellia sinensis rolled and carried to full oxidation before firing ends it: the leaf's own enzymes, meeting air, give it colour, body and a brisk edge. Orthodox whole leaf goes in the pot; CTC, crush, tear and curl, fills most bags and suits anything taken with milk. It is what most guests mean by a hot tea, and the base of the iced tea programme.
taste: Malt, dried fruit and cocoa, a drying astringency down the sides of the tongue, and enough backbone to take milk and sugar without falling apart.

steps: Draw fresh cold water and bring it to a full boil once; never reboil a topped up kettle.
Warm the pot with hot water and tip the rinse out.
Weigh 2 to 3 g of leaf per 6 to 8 oz of water, or one bag per cup and two for a 12 oz pot.
Pour the water on at 200 to 212F (93 to 100C) and start a timer.
Steep 3 to 5 minutes, then pull the bag or basket.
Send milk, lemon and sugar on the side, and warn the table before milk and lemon go in together.
make.ratio: 2 to 3 g of leaf per 6 to 8 oz of water
make.dose: One bag, about 2 g, or 2 to 3 g loose leaf per cup
make.cup: Warmed pot into a cup or mug, 6 to 8 oz

serve: Warm the pot and the cup. Send pot, cup and saucer, a spoon, a small dish for the bag or basket, and the steep time said aloud or a timer on the table. Milk from the fridge, lemon and sugar ride on the side, never in the cup. In a pot, black leaf gives one good steep; brewed gongfu style, short and often, whole leaf gives four or five.
story: In Chinese it is hong cha, red tea, named for the colour of the liquor, while hei cha, literally black tea, is the dark family that microbes ferment. A black leaf darkens because its own enzymes meet air: oxidation, not fermentation. Assam gives malt and body, high grown Ceylon brightness, Kenya the brisk CTC of the tea bag. A guest who orders orange pekoe means plain black tea: the words grade leaf size and tip, not flavour, and have nothing to do with citrus.
guest: A black tea is malty and brisk and takes milk well; would you like milk or lemon on the side, and shall I pull the bag for you?
watch: For a stronger cup give more leaf, not more time: two bags at three minutes, never one at seven, which only adds the drying grip.
Milk and lemon together can curdle in the cup; warn the table or send one of them.
Cloudy iced black tea is usually tea cream, not spoilage: warm a glass and true cream clears, while haze that stays means a dirty urn.
To some guests red tea means rooibos, which is not tea at all; ask which they mean.

recall.prompt: How is a pot of black tea made?
recall.answer: Fresh water at a full boil, 200 to 212F (93 to 100C), over 2 to 3 g of leaf per 6 to 8 oz in a warmed pot, steeped 3 to 5 minutes and pulled. Malty and brisk, it takes milk, lemon or sugar on the side.

quiz.q: What turns a black tea leaf dark during processing?
options: Oxidation by the leaf's own enzymes
Years of ageing in pressed cakes
quiz.explain: Rolling bruises the leaf so its enzymes meet air: oxidation. Microbes do the work only in dark tea, hei cha, such as ripe pu-erh.

quiz.q: A guest asks for a stronger pot of black tea. What is the right fix?
options: The same leaf steeped seven minutes
Leave the bag in the cup
More leaf, the same steep time
Top the pot up with boiling water
quiz.explain: After the first minutes, extra time pulls mostly polyphenols, the drying grip. More leaf at the same time gives strength in the right ratio: two bags at three minutes, never one at seven.

quiz.q: A guest orders an orange pekoe. What are they asking for?
options: A black tea flavoured with orange
A green tea with citrus peel
A herbal blend with dried orange
quiz.explain: Orange pekoe grades the dry leaf by size and tip. It is not a flavour or a type, and the orange has nothing to do with citrus.
